title: Groups: capture, name, or just group
explanation:
Parentheses do two jobs: they **group** part of a pattern (so a quantifier or alternation applies to it), and by default they **capture** the text that part matched.

- `(x)` — capturing group. Captures are numbered by the position of their **left parenthesis**: `match[1]`, `match[2]`, …
- `(?<name>x)` — named capturing group, available as `match.groups.name`. Names make long patterns readable.
- `(?:x)` — non-capturing group: groups without remembering. Use it when you only need grouping, so the capture numbers stay meaningful.

```js
const m = "3x4".match(/^(\d+)x(\d+)$/);
console.log(m[0], m[1], m[2]);                 // 3x4 3 4
const n = "v2.7".match(/^v(?<major>\d+)\.(?<minor>\d+)$/);
console.log(n.groups.major, n.groups.minor);   // 2 7
console.log("nanana batman".match(/^(?:na)+ batman$/).length); // 1 -- no captures, just the full match
```

One trap: `String.prototype.match` with the `g` flag returns only the full matches and **drops the groups**. When you need captures for every match, use `matchAll` (it requires `g`) or call `exec` in a loop.
keyIdeas: `(...)` groups and captures; numbering follows left parentheses.

workedExample.problem: Parse a 24-hour time like `"14:05"` into `{ hour: "14", minute: "05" }` with named groups, rejecting `"9:5"` and `"14:05pm"`.
steps: Each part is exactly two digits: `\d{2}`.
Name the captures so the code reads clearly: `(?<hour>\d{2}):(?<minute>\d{2})`.
Anchor with `^...$` so extra text such as `pm` makes the match fail.
Read the values from `match.groups`; a failed match returns `null`, so check before reading.
workedExample.answer: `/^(?<hour>\d{2}):(?<minute>\d{2})$/` gives `groups.hour === "14"` and `groups.minute === "05"`; the two bad inputs return `null`.

pitfalls: Adding a grouping-only parenthesis and shifting every later capture number; use `(?:...)` for grouping.
Calling `.match(/.../g)` and expecting `[1]` to be a capture — with `g` you get only full matches.
Reading `match.groups.x` without checking for `null` when the pattern didn't match.

citations.quote: Capturing group: Matches x and remembers the match.
In results, matches to capturing groups typically in an array whose members are in the same order as the left parentheses in the capturing group.
Named capturing group: Matches "x" and stores it on the groups property of the returned matches under the name specified by <Name>.
Non-capturing group: Matches "x" but does not remember the match.
String.prototype.match() won't return groups if the /.../g flag is set. However, you can still use String.prototype.matchAll() to get all matches.
